entries.title: Concepts of Health, Health Equity, and Cultural Safety

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/concepts-of-health-and-its-determinants/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj78-1's title and key objectives: 'define and discuss the concepts of health, wellness, illness, disease, and sickness' and 'describe the determinants of health' -- this unit is exactly that definitional and conceptual content, including the Lalonde Report/SDOH framework and the population health model.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/providing-anti-oppressive-health-care/

testable_competencies.definitions: Distinguish disease, illness, sickness, impairment, disability, and handicap, and health equity from health equality.

testable_competencies.cultural_safety: Distinguish cultural humility, cultural safety, cultural awareness, cultural sensitivity, and cultural competency as a spectrum of approaches to culturally appropriate care.

entries.title: Groups Facing Systemic Barriers, Discrimination, and Structural Violence

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj127's key objective explicitly requires the candidate to 'recognize the effects of stigmatization, discrimination, and other forms of oppression on people who have historically experienced and continue to experience health inequities based on race or ethnicity, ... income, ... gender identity ... sexual orientation, weight,' etc. -- this unit's Table 2 (Indigenous Peoples, Black individuals, seniors, people in poverty, people with disabilities, new immigrants, persons experiencing homelessness, refugees, religious minorities, LGBTQI2S individuals, formerly incarcerated persons) is precisely that named set of equity-seeking groups.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The Health Advocate role objective directly matches: 'given a patient, community, or population with health inequities, the candidate will identify the social and structural factors affecting health, describe the impact of these factors, and suggest interventions to address these issues through advocacy' -- this unit's population-specific risk factors and interventions columns are exactly this content.

testable_competencies.recognition: For a given equity-seeking group, identify the systemic barriers, discrimination, and structural factors (not innate characteristics) driving that group's poorer health outcomes.
testable_competencies.screening_for_poverty: Apply the two validated poverty-screening questions and connect patients to appropriate social/financial supports.

entries.title: Indigenous Health in Canada and the Legacy of Colonization

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/indigenous-health/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj78-9's title and key objective: 'given an Indigenous patient, the candidate will demonstrate an awareness of the root causes of the inequitable health care and health outcomes experienced by Indigenous Peoples ... articulate the inherent Indigenous and Treaty Rights ... relevant to the health of Indigenous Peoples' -- this unit's colonization history (residential schools, nutrition trials, TB sanatoriums, coerced sterilization, Sixties Scoop) is exactly that root-causes content.

testable_competencies.historical_context: Identify the major historical mechanisms of colonial harm to Indigenous health in Canada (residential schools, coercive nutrition research, forced relocation to TB sanatoriums, coerced sterilization, the Sixties Scoop) and their documented intergenerational health effects.
testable_competencies.culturally_safe_care: Apply a curiosity-based, culturally humble approach (e.g., asking what the patient needs the physician to know) rather than assuming an Indigenous patient's preferences regarding traditional medicine.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps ELOM's Indigenous Health/Resources in Indigenous Health content (explicitly cross-referenced in-text to ELOM25/ELOM29/ELOM30); this unit covers the population-health historical-determinants angle rather than the ELOM clinical-encounter/consent angle.

entries.title: Disease Prevention: Natural History, Surveillance, and Levels of Prevention

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-3's enabling objectives explicitly require the candidate to 'define the levels of prevention in an individual (clinical) and in a population' and 'understand the importance of disease surveillance ... and be aware of approaches to surveillance' -- this unit is exactly that content (natural history stages, passive/active/sentinel surveillance, Table 3 primordial/primary/secondary/tertiary prevention).

testable_competencies.prevention_levels: Classify a given intervention as primordial, primary, secondary, or tertiary prevention.
testable_competencies.surveillance_types: Distinguish passive, active, and sentinel surveillance by resource intensity and appropriate use case.

entries.title: Screening Principles and Screening Biases

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/interventions-at-the-population-level/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-3's enabling objectives explicitly require the candidate to 'apply the principles of screening, evaluate the utility of a proposed screening intervention, and be able to discuss the potential for lead-time bias and length-prevalence bias' -- naming the exact two biases this unit covers.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/periodic-health-encounter-preventive-health-advice/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Screening is a core component of the periodic health encounter obj74's scope (age/sex-specific screening investigations), though obj74 is framed around the whole preventive encounter rather than screening theory/bias specifically.

testable_competencies.screening_vs_diagnosis: Distinguish the purpose of a screening test (detect early disease/risk in asymptomatic people) from a diagnostic test (confirm disease in symptomatic/screen-positive people).
testable_competencies.bias_recognition: Given a screening-outcomes scenario, identify whether an apparent survival/prevalence benefit reflects lead-time bias or length-time bias rather than a true mortality benefit.
testable_competencies.screening_criteria: Apply Wilson-Jungner-type ideal screening criteria (disease burden, natural history understood, effective early treatment, acceptable/sensitive/cost-effective test) to judge whether a proposed screening program is appropriate.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-3's enabling objectives explicitly require the candidate to 'describe the application of health promotion,' 'describe one or more models of behaviour change, including predisposing, enabling, and reinforcing factors,' and 'describe strategies for community needs assessments, health education, community engagement, and health promotion' -- naming this unit's content directly.

testable_competencies.ottawa_charter: Apply the Ottawa Charter's five health-promotion strategies (healthy public policy, supportive environments, community action, personal skills, reoriented health services) to a population-health scenario.
testable_competencies.behaviour_change: Apply the Health Belief Model (perceived susceptibility/severity/benefits/barriers, cues to action, self-efficacy) and the Stages of Change Model (precontemplation through maintenance) to a patient behaviour-change scenario.
testable_competencies.risk_vs_harm_reduction: Distinguish risk reduction from harm reduction interventions.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-2's enabling objectives explicitly require the candidate to 'describe the concepts of incidence, prevalence, attack rates, and case fatality rates, calculating them, and discussing the principles of standardization' -- naming this unit's exact content.

entries.title: Measures of Mortality and Disease Burden

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Assessing and measuring health status at the population level
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/assessing-and-measuring-health-status-at-the-population-level/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls within obj78-2's enabling objective to describe and calculate 'measures of health, disease' at the population level; life expectancy, crude/infant/maternal mortality rates, PYLL, DALY, and QALY are the chapter's standard population mortality/burden measures used to fulfill that objective.

testable_competencies.mortality_measures: Calculate and interpret crude death rate, infant mortality rate, and maternal mortality rate.

entries.title: Population, Sampling Methods, and Sample Size

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Assessing and measuring health status at the population level
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/assessing-and-measuring-health-status-at-the-population-level/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-2's enabling objectives explicitly list 'sampling' among the measures of health/disease/sampling the candidate must be able to discuss when critically appraising research findings -- this unit is the population/sample/sampling-method/sample-size foundation for that appraisal skill.

testable_competencies.sampling_methods: Distinguish probability sampling methods (simple/systematic/stratified random, cluster) from non-probability methods (convenience, snowball) and identify an appropriate method for a given research scenario.
testable_competencies.sample_size_effects: Explain that increasing sample size improves precision (narrower CIs) and reduces Type I/II error probability, but does not reduce bias or confounding.

entries.title: Bias and Confounding in Epidemiologic Studies

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Assessing and measuring health status at the population level
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/assessing-and-measuring-health-status-at-the-population-level/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-2's enabling objectives explicitly list 'bias, confounding' among the measurement issues the candidate must incorporate when critically appraising research findings -- this unit is exactly that content (selection bias subtypes, information bias subtypes, confounding and its control).

testable_competencies.bias_subtypes: Given a study description, identify the specific type of selection bias (Berkson's, non-response, loss-to-follow-up) or information bias (recall, interviewer, observer) present.
testable_competencies.confounding: Distinguish a confounder from a mediator, and identify randomization, stratification, matching, or regression modelling as methods to control confounding.

entries.title: Interpreting Diagnostic Test Results (Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values, Likelihood Ratios)

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Assessing and measuring health status at the population level
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/assessing-and-measuring-health-status-at-the-population-level/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-2's enabling objectives explicitly list 'sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value' among the measurement issues required for critical appraisal -- this unit is exactly that content plus likelihood ratios and pre-/post-test probability.

testable_competencies.sens_spec_calc: Calculate and interpret sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV from a 2x2 table, and explain why PPV/NPV (unlike sensitivity/specificity) depend on disease prevalence.
testable_competencies.likelihood_ratios: Use a likelihood ratio and a Fagan nomogram (or the odds form) to convert a pre-test probability into a post-test probability given a test result.
testable_competencies.spin_snout: Apply the SPIN (specific test rules IN) and SNOUT (sensitive test rules OUT) heuristics to select an appropriate test for ruling in vs. ruling out a diagnosis.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Administration of effective health programs at the population level

entries.title: Qualitative vs. Quantitative Research Approaches

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Assessing and measuring health status at the population level
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/assessing-and-measuring-health-status-at-the-population-level/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls within obj78-2's general scope of critically appraising research findings and describing 'types of data and common components (both qualitative and quantitative) used in creating a community health needs assessment'; MODERATE because the qualitative-vs-quantitative framing itself (PICO, bottom-up vs. top-down question formulation) is not separately named in the objective's enabling-objective text.

testable_competencies.approach_selection: Distinguish qualitative from quantitative research approaches by their typical research questions, sampling logic, and data type, and recognize PICO as a quantitative question-formulation framework.

entries.title: Observational Study Designs (Cohort, Case-Control, Cross-Sectional, Ecological)

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Assessing and measuring health status at the population level
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/assessing-and-measuring-health-status-at-the-population-level/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-2's enabling objectives explicitly require the candidate to critically appraise research with reference to 'characteristics of study designs (randomized controlled trial, cohort, case-control, cross-sectional)' -- naming three of this unit's four designs directly (ecological is the fourth, closely related design presented in the same source table).

testable_competencies.design_identification: Given a study description, identify whether it is an ecological, cross-sectional, case-control, or cohort design.
testable_competencies.design_tradeoffs: For a given research question, select the most appropriate observational design and identify its characteristic strengths (e.g., cohort providing incidence/RR) and vulnerabilities (e.g., case-control's recall bias, ecological fallacy).
testable_competencies.ecological_fallacy: Recognize an ecological fallacy when population-level associations are incorrectly extrapolated to individuals.

entries.title: Experimental Study Designs (Randomized Controlled Trials)

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Assessing and measuring health status at the population level
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/assessing-and-measuring-health-status-at-the-population-level/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-2's enabling objectives explicitly name 'randomized controlled trial' as a study design characteristic the candidate must appraise -- this unit is the RCT-specific design content (randomization, blinding levels, advantages/disadvantages).

testable_competencies.rct_features: Identify the key methodological features of an RCT (randomization, blinding level, control group) and explain why randomization is uniquely able to control for both measured and unmeasured confounding.
testable_competencies.rct_limitations: Recognize situations where an RCT is not feasible or ethical (e.g., harmful exposures) and identify threats to RCT validity (contamination, co-intervention, loss to follow-up, poor generalizability).

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls within obj78-2's general scope of critically appraising research findings and study characteristics; MODERATE because meta-analysis/systematic review/scoping review are not individually named in the objective's enabling-objective text, unlike the primary study designs it does name.

testable_competencies.synthesis_design_selection: Distinguish a meta-analysis (quantitative pooling), a systematic review (rigorous narrative synthesis), and a scoping review (mapping the literature without a single synthesized answer), and recognize publication bias and study heterogeneity as key meta-analysis limitations.
testable_competencies.analysis_strategy: Distinguish intention-to-treat analysis from per-protocol analysis.

entries.title: Distributions and Descriptive Statistics

entries.title: Statistical Hypothesis Testing, Error Types, and Confidence Intervals

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Assessing and measuring health status at the population level
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/assessing-and-measuring-health-status-at-the-population-level/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls within obj78-2's general scope of critically appraising research findings, including 'error' among the listed measurement issues; MODERATE because Type I/II error, statistical power, p-values, and confidence intervals are not individually named in the objective's enabling-objective text, unlike sensitivity/specificity/bias/confounding, which are.

testable_competencies.confidence_intervals: Interpret a 95% confidence interval and explain how a wider interval reflects greater uncertainty for the same point estimate.

entries.title: Choosing an Appropriate Statistical Test

testable_competencies.test_selection_awareness: Recognize, at a conceptual level, that the choice of statistical test (e.g., t-test vs. ANOVA vs. chi-squared vs. regression) depends on the number and type (continuous/categorical) of variables being compared.

entries.zero_question_reason: Per chapter-scoping instructions, specialist statistical-test-selection mechanics exceed the testable depth expected of a graduating medical student; MCCQE difficulty in this domain should come from interpreting evidence (SU-PH-13/14/16/17) rather than performing or selecting specialist statistical tests. Retained as a study unit for source-traceability and conceptual completeness only.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-5's key objective directly requires the candidate to 'define characteristics of an outbreak and know how to recognize one when it occurs' -- this unit's outbreak/endemic/epidemic/pandemic definitions and attack-rate/CFR/R0 measures are exactly that content.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Assessing and measuring health status at the population level
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/assessing-and-measuring-health-status-at-the-population-level/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-2's enabling objectives explicitly list 'attack rates, and case fatality rates' among the measures the candidate must describe and calculate -- directly corroborating this unit's formulas.

testable_competencies.terminology: Distinguish outbreak, endemic, epidemic, and pandemic by scale and expected baseline frequency.
testable_competencies.outbreak_measures: Calculate and interpret attack rate, secondary attack rate, case-fatality rate, and basic reproduction number (R0), and distinguish case-fatality rate from the general mortality rate.

entries.title: Steps to Control an Outbreak and Epidemic Curves

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/outbreak-management/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-5's key objective and enabling objectives directly require the candidate to 'describe and understand the main steps in outbreak prevention and management' and 'demonstrate skills in effective outbreak management' -- this unit's ten-step outbreak-investigation approach is exactly that content.

testable_competencies.investigation_steps: Sequence the steps of an outbreak investigation (confirm the outbreak, verify diagnosis, define a case, find cases/line list, descriptive epidemiology, generate/evaluate hypotheses, implement control measures, communicate, continue surveillance).
testable_competencies.epidemic_curve_interpretation: Interpret an epidemic curve to distinguish a point-source, continuous-source, or propagated-source outbreak.

entries.title: Communicable Disease Control and Infection Prevention and Control Practices

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/outbreak-management/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-5's enabling objectives explicitly require the candidate to 'implement environmental control measures when the outbreak is due to an infectious agent' and 'describe infection control practices, including immunoprophylaxis and chemoprophylaxis' and 'describe appropriate approaches ... including isolation and quarantine measures' -- this unit's Routine Practices/Additional Precautions/IHR content is exactly that.

testable_competencies.epidemiology_triad: Apply the host-agent-environment epidemiology triad framework to identify a communicable-disease control intervention target.
testable_competencies.precautions_selection: Given a pathogen's transmission route, select the appropriate Additional Precautions (contact, droplet, contact+droplet, or airborne) beyond Routine Practices.

entries.title: Environmental Health Framework, Jurisdiction, and Risk Assessment

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/environment/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-6's enabling objectives explicitly require the candidate to 'identify common environmental hazards and classify them into the appropriate category of chemical, biological, physical, and radiation,' 'describe the steps in an environmental risk assessment,' and 'be aware of local, regional, provincial, and national regulatory agencies' -- this unit is exactly that framework, jurisdiction table, and HIRA steps.

testable_competencies.hazard_classification: Classify an environmental exposure into its hazard category (chemical, biological, physical, radiation) and reservoir (air, water, soil, food).
testable_competencies.risk_assessment_steps: Apply the four-step Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment framework (hazard identification, dose-response, exposure assessment, risk characterization) to an environmental exposure scenario.
testable_competencies.environmental_history: Take a structured environmental exposure history using the CH2OPD2 mnemonic.

entries.title: Air, Water, and Soil Environmental Hazards

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/environment/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-6's enabling objectives explicitly require the candidate to 'identify the common hazards that are found in air, water, soil, and food' -- this unit is exactly the air/water/soil portion of that content.

testable_competencies.hazard_recognition: Given an environmental exposure scenario (e.g., contaminated well water, urban smog, contaminated soil near a former industrial site), identify the likely hazard category and associated health effect.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-6's enabling objectives explicitly require the candidate to 'identify the common hazards that are found in air, water, soil, and food' -- this unit is the food-hazard portion of that content.

testable_competencies.foodborne_pathogen_recognition: Given a food source and clinical presentation, identify the likely biological food-borne contaminant (Salmonella, Campylobacter, E. coli O157:H7, Listeria, Clostridium botulinum, prion) from Table 12.

entries.title: Environmental Racism (Grassy Narrows and Africville)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/indigenous-health/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls within obj78-9's scope of Indigenous health root causes; the Grassy Narrows mercury-poisoning case is a named, canonical Canadian example of an environmental determinant of Indigenous health inequity directly matching obj78-9's 'root causes of the inequitable health care and health outcomes experienced by Indigenous Peoples.'

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/black-health/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls within obj78-13's scope of Black Health; the Africville case is a named, canonical Canadian example of environmental racism against a Black community, matching obj78-13's focus on the 'complexities of Black health and well-being' including historical and structural factors.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/environment/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-6's general environmental-hazard framework applies to both cases as concrete instances of unequal environmental hazard exposure, though obj78-6's own enabling-objective text does not name racism/equity explicitly.

testable_competencies.environmental_racism_recognition: Define environmental racism and recognize Grassy Narrows (Indigenous, mercury contamination) and Africville (Black community, industrial siting and forced relocation) as the chapter's named Canadian examples.

entries.title: Climate Change, Health Impacts, and Public Health Response

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/health-and-the-climate-crisis/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj78-11's title and key objectives: 'discuss the effect of climate change on the health of the population' and 'describe how physicians can address climate issues in small-scale ... and large-scale settings' -- this unit's climate-health-hazard list and mitigation/adaptation framework is exactly that content.

testable_competencies.climate_health_hazards: Identify the mechanism by which a given climate-related hazard (extreme weather, air quality, vector range shift, food/water insecurity) produces a specific health effect.
testable_competencies.mitigation_vs_adaptation: Distinguish mitigation (reducing emissions to slow climate change) from adaptation (preparing health systems for climate change's effects).

entries.title: Disaster Preparedness, Emergency Response, and Recovery

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Disaster preparedness, emergency response, and recovery
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/disaster-preparedness-emergency-response-and-recovery/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj78-10's title and key objectives: 'discuss the defining characteristics of a disaster,' 'describe approaches to disaster prevention and mitigation,' 'develop an emergency response plan,' and 'assist with the recovery operation' -- this unit's disaster-hazard taxonomy and prevention-mitigation-preparedness-response-recovery framework is exactly that content.

testable_competencies.hazard_classification: Classify a disaster's causal hazard as natural, human-system, or multi-level.
testable_competencies.response_framework: Distinguish prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery as sequential phases of disaster management, and identify the role of an Emergency Response Plan, Incident Management System, Emergency Operations Centre, and Continuity of Operations Plan.

entries.title: Occupational Medicine Overview and Occupational History Taking

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/work-related-health-issues/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-8's key objective directly matches: 'given a patient with a health problem, the candidate will evaluate the possible workplace etiological factors ... perform a history and focused physical examination to identify the illness and determine the possible relationship of symptoms to work' -- this unit's WHACS occupational-history mnemonic and the formal exposure-identification/assessment/temporal-relationship framework is exactly that skill.

testable_competencies.occupational_history: Take a structured occupational history (current/previous duties, exposure identification and assessment, temporal relationship to symptoms, co-worker symptoms, non-work exposures) to determine whether a presenting condition is work-related.
testable_competencies.occupational_vs_nonoccupational: Recognize that occupational disease often looks clinically identical to non-occupational disease and may go unrecognized without a deliberate occupational history.

entries.title: Occupational Hazards by Category (Physical, Chemical, Biological, Psychosocial, Ergonomic, Safety)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/work-related-health-issues/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-8's own causal_conditions list names exactly these hazard categories: 'ergonomic hazards ... chemical hazards ... physical hazards ... biological hazards ... psychological and work organization hazards' -- a near-verbatim match to this unit's Table 13 taxonomy (which additionally separates out safety hazards).

testable_competencies.hazard_category_recognition: Given an occupational exposure and clinical presentation (e.g., noise -> hearing loss, benzene -> AML, asbestos -> mesothelioma, silica -> silicosis), classify the hazard category and identify the associated health effect.

entries.title: Workplace Legislation and Workers' Compensation

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/work-related-health-issues/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-8's enabling objectives include advising 'the patient on workers compensation' as part of the management plan for a work-related health problem; MODERATE because obj78-8 is framed clinically around one patient's case rather than the legislative/regulatory framework (WHMIS, OHSA, WSIB) this unit covers in general.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/legal-ethical-and-organizational-aspects-of-medicine/legal-system/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj121-5's enabling objectives require the candidate to 'recognize the various sources of laws in Canada ... as they apply to the practice of medicine' and 'identify situations in which consultation, reporting, or referral is appropriate'; this unit's provincial-vs-federal workplace-legislation jurisdiction and WSIB no-fault framework is a specific instance of that general legal-system awareness.

testable_competencies.legislative_framework: Identify the jurisdiction (provincial vs. federally-regulated industry) governing a workplace, and describe the no-fault principle of workers' compensation insurance (WSIB-type boards).
testable_competencies.worker_rights: Identify a worker's four core rights under Canadian occupational health and safety legislation: to know, to participate, to refuse unsafe work, and (for certified workers) to stop work.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps ELOM's Legal System content (obj121-5); this unit covers the occupational-health-specific legislative and compensation framework rather than the general legal system.

entries.title: Workplace Health Promotion

testable_competencies.health_promotion_awareness: Recognize workplace health promotion as a voluntary, non-legislated employer strategy distinct from the legislated primary/secondary/tertiary prevention framework (SU-PH-39).

entries.zero_question_reason: Thin, largely definitional content (a one-sentence contrast with legislated prevention) with no distinct MCC objective evidence and low independent testable value beyond the contrast already captured in SU-PH-39; retained as a study unit for source-traceability only.

entries.title: Workplace Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Prevention

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/work-related-health-issues/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-8's enabling objectives directly match this unit's three-level structure: 'identify protective equipment being used and environmental controls' (primary), 'physiologic and/or functional assessments (e.g., PFTs, audiograms)' (secondary), and 'determine whether the patient should be assigned to different work, or stop work' plus 'determine follow up care' (tertiary).

testable_competencies.hierarchy_of_controls: Apply the hierarchy of controls (elimination > substitution > engineering controls > administrative controls > PPE, most to least effective) to select the best primary-prevention intervention for an occupational hazard.
testable_competencies.medical_surveillance: Identify an appropriate secondary-prevention medical surveillance test for a given occupational exposure (e.g., audiograms for noise, spirometry for dust exposure, blood lead testing for lead exposure).
testable_competencies.return_to_work: Apply the restrictions/limitations/abilities/tolerance framework to a tertiary-prevention return-to-work planning scenario.

entries.title: Mandatory Reporting: Reportable Diseases

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Assessing and measuring health status at the population level
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/assessing-and-measuring-health-status-at-the-population-level/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj78-2's enabling objectives explicitly require the candidate to discuss 'surveillance systems and the role of physicians and public health in reporting and responding to disease' -- this unit's legal reporting duty and reportable-disease list is exactly that physician-reporting-role content.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/legal-ethical-and-organizational-aspects-of-medicine/legal-system/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj121-5's enabling objectives explicitly list 'public health' as an example situation in which 'consultation, reporting, or referral is appropriate' -- directly matching this unit's mandatory-reporting legal obligation.

testable_competencies.reporting_duty: Recognize that physicians in Canada have a mandatory, provincially-legislated duty to report specified diseases to public health, that failure to report can result in licence suspension, and identify the reasons reporting is required (outbreak control, threat containment, treatable/preventable disease, surveillance).

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps ELOM's general confidentiality/reporting-duty content; this unit covers the public-health-specific mandatory disease-reporting obligation.

entries.title: Other Mandatory Reporting Obligations

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/legal-ethical-and-organizational-aspects-of-medicine/legal-system/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj121-5's enabling objectives explicitly list 'child protection services' and 'public health' as example situations requiring reporting/referral -- directly matching this unit's non-disease mandatory-reporting obligations (child abuse to CAS, births/deaths to the Registrar General/Coroner, gunshot wounds to police, LTC-resident abuse, unfit-to-drive/unfit-to-fly).

testable_competencies.reporting_triggers: For a given clinical scenario (suspected child abuse, a gunshot wound, a patient with a medical condition impairing safe driving or flying, suspected abuse of a long-term-care resident, a death of unclear cause), identify the correct mandatory-reporting trigger and the correct recipient body (CAS, police, Ministry of Transportation, Registrar/Coroner, Retirement Homes Regulatory Authority).

entries.cross_discipline_note: This grab-bag of legal reporting duties overlaps substantially with ELOM's general confidentiality/reporting-obligations content and with Pediatrics' child-abuse-recognition content; per the chapter-scoping instructions, PRIMARY_OWNER/CROSS_LINK/DISTINCT_CONTEXT is not finalized here pending the global cross-chapter ownership audit.

entries.title: Landmark Preventive Medicine and Screening Trials

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/interventions-at-the-population-level/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls within obj78-3's general scope of evidence for population-level prevention interventions (screening, immunization); MODERATE because obj78-3's enabling-objective text does not name these specific trials, though the trials themselves are the chapter's worked evidentiary examples for screening (SU-PH-07) and prevention (SU-PH-06) concepts.

testable_competencies.trial_evidence_recall: Given a description of one of the six landmark trials' methods and results (Swedish Two-County/mammography, MASS/AAA screening, COLONPREV/colonoscopy vs. FIT, NLST/lung cancer CT screening, VAXICOL/influenza vaccination of staff, BNT162b2/COVID-19 vaccine), identify the trial's principal conclusion.
